market_response.title: Adam opens confidential Model II cooperation talks
market_response.description: After Aurelia launch and growing dealer sales, Adam demonstrates Abacus and proposes an official Model II CP/M configuration plus FlexiBUS in return for an AION-funded Abacus adaptation. Talks occur during the scenario early-design window; no historical design-freeze date is asserted. Confidential talks have no immediate mass-market demand effect.

market_response.title: Tandy, Logix, DRI and AION sign Model II cooperation agreement
market_response.description: Tandy commits to officially selling/supporting CP/M and a qualified FlexiBUS option for Model II, supplies engineering access and distributes Abacus. DRI supplies CP/M and required platform services. Logix supplies interface documentation, reference engineering and initial chips. AION funds the port, corrects incompatibilities, qualifies and maintains the Model II edition. Tandy keeps native video, keyboard, disk architecture, legacy ports, branding, sales and first-line support. No Logix video or CP/M-6502 commitment.

market_response.title: Model II compatibility design baseline agreed
market_response.description: Reserve an internal option-board slot and interface/power budget before the scenario design baseline is closed. Freeze CP/M BIOS responsibilities, native display/keyboard adapter and the FlexiBUS connector plan. This review is an invented alternate-history engineering milestone, not a claim about the real Model II freeze date.

market_response.title: Model II CP/M and Abacus prototype review
market_response.description: Review prototype CP/M boot, Tandy disk/printer BIOS, native TUI adapter and Abacus document interchange. Resolve ROM/banking assumptions and measure available RAM on the 64 KB target. FlexiBUS prototype is specific to the Tandy bus, not a plug-in S-100 card.

market_response.title: Model II announced with planned CP/M, FlexiBUS and Abacus offering
market_response.description: Publicly announce Model II and the planned officially supported CP/M/Abacus configuration and FlexiBUS option. Preserve the historical late-May announcement window, June NCC demonstrations and October US delivery window. Announcements and orders are not completed computer or Abacus sales.

market_response.title: Model II CP/M, FlexiBUS and Abacus demonstrated at NCC
market_response.description: Demonstrate Abacus using the native Model II display/keyboard, a CP/M disk build and qualified prototype FlexiBUS peripherals. Distinguish demonstrations from customer releases; announce an autumn supported 64 KB configuration. No Logix video subsystem is required.

market_response.title: Supported Model II CP/M and Abacus configuration released
market_response.description: Scenario customer release within the historical October US shipping window: supported 64 KB CP/M configuration, Model II Abacus and the separately supported FlexiBUS option. Release follows disk, printing, save/reopen, native UI and interface qualification; publish resource limits. October 15 is a scenario-selected day. OEM economics and Tandy system prices are not inferred from Aurelia retail prices.

market_response.title: Apple coordinates business-software recruitment
market_response.description: Respond to Aurelia with a coordinated search for accounting, spreadsheet and database partners, engineering access and demonstration systems. Disk II development already predates Aurelia; this is a change in software/commercial priority, not the invention of disk support.

market_response.title: Apple business-dealer demonstration programme
market_response.description: Prepare complete-system quotations, repeatable business-workflow demonstrations and introductory customer lessons. Initial implementation is selective, not an instantly nationwide training network.

market_response.title: Apple promotes complete business configurations
market_response.description: Participating dealers promote Apple II/Disk II business configurations, demonstrations and introductory lessons; Apple pursues spreadsheet distribution/development support separately from Peachtree accounting. No completed VisiCalc release or finished March 1980 Apple–Peachtree package is pulled into spring 1979.

market_response.title: Apple reviews successor-product compatibility requirements
market_response.description: Competitive review increases priority for protecting existing software, peripherals and customer data in successor plans. This is a requirements decision, not a guaranteed technical fix or early Lisa/GUI shipment. Apple keeps its independent hardware roadmap.

market_response.title: IBM software sourcing review exposes schedule gap
market_response.description: CP/M-86 does not exist. DRI prioritises CP/M-80/TUI, AIONix and PRO. Adam owns 30% of independent DRI and Logix competes with IBM, making schedule and strategic dependence concerns substantial. Paterson never creates QDOS; Microsoft cannot acquire the historical SCP product. IBM investigates independently commissioned disk-OS alternatives.

market_response.title: IBM funds an alternative OS delivery programme
market_response.description: After evaluating suppliers, fund substitute OS work and stabilise application interfaces. Supplier identity and OS name remain unresolved. Hardware development proceeds; development, utilities, application ports and service preparation now determine commercial timing.

market_response.title: IBM business-software qualification delays commercial release
market_response.description: OS integration, application qualification and support delay the substantially ready hardware. Central planning assumes a March 1982 commercial release; this is a scenario forecast, not historical fact or a CP/M-86 rescue. Qualification slippage is represented by the demand bounds.

market_response.title: Tandy reinforces native-video CP/M business bundles
market_response.description: Sustain the existing native-video CP/M/Abacus agreement. Improve dealer training and integrated business bundles; independent Tandy hardware sales are excluded from Logix revenue.

market_response.title: Artemis trials favour selective native application ports
market_response.description: Developers prioritise profitable C/TUI applications, test files and arithmetic, and retain CP/M editions. Source compatibility lowers work but does not make Z80 binaries run natively on ERA.

market_response.title: Independent vendors qualify interface adapters
market_response.description: Independent vendors developed printer, serial, storage and expansion adapters against the published FlexiBUS, monitor and internal-card interfaces. Vendors validated electrical behaviour, protocol conformance and supported configurations. AION offered optional certification for vendors seeking its tested-compatibility designation.

market_response.title: Portable CP/M offerings compete for business buyers
market_response.description: Osborne-class bundled portable systems make CP/M software libraries and total package cost important. Their historic market segment remains plausible; exact alternative-world volume and component supply are not asserted.

market_response.title: Dealers and BPI gate server sales on recovery tests
market_response.description: Run multi-client authentication, locking, backup and crash-recovery pilots. PRO shipments from July remain conditional. Five-megabyte storage confines early Team Edition deployments to small repositories; larger storage remains unpriced and contributes no forecast revenue.

market_response.title: Recession prompts staged purchases and leaner dealer stock
market_response.description: Use the historical July 1981–November 1982 recession as a demand constraint. Buyers stage network installations and dealers limit inventory. Revised quarterly demand replaces uninterrupted 4% monthly growth.

market_response.title: Unix suppliers counter integrated team development
market_response.description: Workstation and multiuser suppliers emphasise mature tools, storage, support and existing Unix software. They can bundle editors, compilers and revision tools; an equally integrated modern collaboration product is not assumed to appear instantly.

market_response.title: DRI starts independently licensed 68k AIONix port work
market_response.description: Non-ERA porting rights become effective. Fund an eight-engineer feasibility effort, credit half of retained DRI payroll and add prototype validation. Select suitable external-MMU hardware and investigate restartable faults; no released port or licence receipts assumed in 1982.

market_response.title: 80286 opens a protected x86 feasibility path
market_response.description: February 1982 availability of 80286 protected mode changes feasibility. Segmented memory, toolchains, drivers, target hardware and validation still require work. No full AIONix port to 8086/8088, immediate 286 release or port revenue is assumed.

market_response.title: IBM launches its independently commissioned disk-OS platform
market_response.description: Central scenario date, conditional on qualification: launch a business PC with a substitute independently commissioned disk OS and an initially narrower application portfolio. Supplier and OS name remain unspecified. Brand, service and dealer reach win buyers; no CP/M-86, QDOS acquisition or immediate mature MS-DOS ecosystem.

market_response.title: 68k OEMs assess an independent AIONix option
market_response.description: Tandy and other 68k vendors examine DRI licensing and reference hardware. Memory protection, fault restart, drivers and commercial support are gates. Assessment is not a shipping product or a signed volume commitment.

market_response.title: Spreadsheet and business software competition intensifies
market_response.description: Microsoft can pursue languages, Xenix and Multiplan-class products while recruiting replacement engineering talent. Logix ports depend on business terms and target testing; historical SoftCard timing is not copied after Paterson recruitment.

market_response.title: Independent compatibility and developer support review
market_response.description: Publish adapter and C/TUI conformance results and compatibility fixes. Successful small-team references support demand, while larger repositories still require separately qualified storage. Market estimates remain forecast ranges.
